=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are clearly attached at the same node, forming a radial arrangement around the stem, with attachment points visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are arranged in tight groups at nodes, with no long internodes between leaf clusters)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade attached to the stem)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (leaf margins are smooth, without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaves are broadest near the middle, tapering gradually to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tips are sharply pointed)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf bases taper to a narrow point, forming a wedge shape)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (primary veins extend from the midrib to the margin, with secondary veins branching off the midrib)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible, running perpendicular to the midrib, with high density)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, rugose (leaf surface is glossy and has a wrinkled or textured appearance)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or trichomes on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are short, not exceeding the width of the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles are round and cylindrical in cross-section)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and rigid, with visible bark texture)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: dark green to brownish-green (stem is dark green with some brownish tones, especially in older sections)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): ridged (stem surface has longitudinal ridges or grooves, not smooth or lenticellate)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate or latex visible from stem or leaves)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base; pulvinus not present)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: Multiple images show the same seedling from different angles, confirming consistent whorled leaf arrangement and simple leaf morphology. Some leaves exhibit minor holes and margin damage, likely from environmental factors. The leaf surface is consistently shiny and rugose, with pinnate venation and short petioles. The stem is woody, ridged, and dark green to brownish-green. No stipules, latex, or tendrils are visible. The leaf base is cuneate, apex acute, and margins entire. Damage is noted as holes and slight margin irregularities without inferring cause. All traits are observed without speculation on family, genus, or species.
